diagnoses.preserve: The tool customizes the beginning of a Git commit hash; the page describes hexadecimal characters and wildcard placeholders.
diagnoses.problem: “Simple” is an unsupported ease-of-use judgment, and “whatever you want” overstates the available prefix choices described later on the page.
diagnoses.quote: With this simple tool, you can change the start of your git commit hashes to whatever you want.

diagnoses.preserve: The tool repeatedly changes whitespace in commit messages until the hash satisfies the requested prefix.
diagnoses.problem: “Good hash” leaves the stopping condition vague even though the surrounding instructions define it as matching the requested prefix.
diagnoses.quote: keeps trying new messages until it finds a good hash.

diagnoses.preserve: Whether CPU performance is adequate depends on the intended use; retain the separate, laptop-specific measurement of about 20x slower.
diagnoses.problem: “There's a good chance” asserts an unspecified likelihood of acceptable performance, while the extended qualification never identifies a workload or adequacy threshold.
diagnoses.quote: but depending on what you're planning to use the tool for, there's a good chance it's fast enough anyway.

diagnoses.preserve: The older versions are slower than the current version and are unmaintained.
diagnoses.problem: “Drastically” assigns an unsupported magnitude to the slowdown. The page's CPU/GPU comparison does not establish performance differences for these older branches.
diagnoses.quote: Note that these older versions are drastically slower than the current version, and are also unmaintained.

diagnoses.preserve: SHA256 use is presented as uncommon, with uncertainty about any particular reader's repository.
diagnoses.problem: The reader's uncertainty is used as evidence of the repository's object format. The page's general rarity claim does not establish that inference.
diagnoses.quote: If you're wondering whether your repository uses sha256, then it probably doesn't.

diagnoses.preserve: At the time of writing, the feature is experimental and its use is described as rare.
diagnoses.problem: “Highly” and “very” amplify the maturity and adoption claims without supporting evidence; “experimental” was already established in the linked format description.
diagnoses.quote: At the time of writing, this is a highly experimental feature and is very rarely used.
